title: Denial of Auto Insurance Coverage – Policy Nonrenewal
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
190th JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-45678-H

JANE ELIZABETH MASON (f/k/a Jane Elizabeth Whitfield), Plaintiff,
vs.
PROTECTIVE SHIELD INSURANCE COMPANY, Defendant.

NOTICE OF DENIAL OF COVERAGE AND NONRENEWAL

TO: Jane Elizabeth Mason
1203 Elmview Drive, Houston, Texas 77002
Phone: (713) 555-0199
Email: jane.mason@emailprovider.com

Date of Birth: born on March 14, 1971

RE: Policy No. 7-882-99123A

Dear Ms. Mason:

This letter is to inform you that Protective Shield Insurance Company has determined that your automobile insurance policy is denied for coverage of the accident occurring on January 15, 2024, and that your policy will not be renewed. Our decision is based on the following facts and applicable law.

On January 15, 2024, you were involved in a single-vehicle collision on Interstate 10 near downtown Houston. Your vehicle, a 2021 Honda Accord, struck a guardrail. You reported the accident to our claims department on January 16, 2024. Our investigation revealed that at the time of the accident, the vehicle was being operated by your minor son, A.B., aged 15, without your permission or a valid driver’s license. Under the terms of your policy, coverage is excluded for losses arising from unauthorized use by a household member who is not listed as a driver. Moreover, your policy contains a material misrepresentation: you stated on your application that no household member under the age of 18 would operate the vehicle, which was false. This misrepresentation voids coverage ab initio.

Pursuant to Texas Insurance Code § 441.002, an insurer may deny coverage for material misrepresentation. The Texas Supreme Court, in the case of Gomez v. Allstate Indemnity Co., 514 S.W.3d 242 (Tex. 2017), held that a misrepresentation that increases the risk of loss permits the insurer to rescind the policy. See also In re State Farm Lloyds, 520 S.W.3d 602 (Tex. 2018) (discussing rescission for misrepresentation). Further, your policy explicitly excludes coverage for any person operating the vehicle without a reasonable belief that they are entitled to do so. The minor A.B. did not have such a belief.

Additionally, your policy contains a provision that permits nonrenewal if the insured or any person who resides in the household has been convicted of driving without a license or causing a material increase in risk. A.B. was charged with driving without a license, and you failed to notify us of this risk factor. Therefore, your policy will not be renewed effective February 1, 2025, as permitted by Texas Insurance Code § 195.002.

You have the right to file suit within 60 days of receipt of this letter. Any questions should be directed to our legal counsel, Margaret L. Chu, at (713) 555-0123, or by email at m.chu@protectiveshield.com. Our company maintains its principal offices at 500 Main Street, Houston, Texas 77002.

Sincerely,

Protective Shield Insurance Company
By: Raymond T. Holmes, Claims Manager

Enclosures: Policy excerpts, claim file summary

Subscribed and sworn to before me this 20th day of February, 2024.
Notary Public, State of Texas

cc: Margaret L. Chu, Esq.
    Judge Patricia O. Delgado (presiding in related mediation case number 24-0001-M) – referred to as Judge Delgado.

title: Denial of Homeowner’s Insurance – Flood Exclusion
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS
261st JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. D-1-GN-24-00392

ROBERT J. KING, SR., Plaintiff,
vs.
LONE STAR MUTUAL INSURANCE COMPANY, Defendant.

NOTICE OF DENIAL OF CLAIM – NO COVERAGE

TO: Robert J. King, Sr.
4521 Riverbend Lane, Apt. 3C, Austin, Texas 78701
Phone: (713) 555-2201
Email: rking.sr@fastmail.com

Social Security Number: 456-78-1234 (last four digits of claim record)

Date of Loss: March 18, 2024

Dear Mr. King:

This letter is to advise you that your claim for water damage occurring on March 18, 2024, at your residence located at 4521 Riverbend Lane is denied. The cause of the damage was rising water from the Colorado River, which constitutes a flood. Your homeowner’s policy, number HD-7789-01-2024, specifically excludes flood damage. You do not have a flood insurance endorsement, nor did you purchase a separate flood policy through the National Flood Insurance Program.

Our investigation, conducted by adjuster Angela M. Torres, confirmed that the water entered your home from the exterior due to the river overflowing. This is a surface water event. Under the policy, “loss caused by flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, overflow of any body of water, or spray from any of these, whether driven by wind or not” is excluded. See Texas Insurance Code § 2001.103. The Texas Court of Appeals, in the case of Hendricks v. Travelers Indemnity, 492 S.W.3d 718 (Tex. App.—Austin 2016, pet. denied), held that similar “water damage” exclusions are enforceable. See also In re State Farm Lloyds, 526 S.W.3d 587 (Tex. 2017) (upholding flood exclusion).

Furthermore, your application listed your residence as being in Flood Zone X (low risk), which is what you represented. However, after the loss, FEMA updated the maps showing your property is in Flood Zone AE. You argue that Lone Star Mutual should have advised you to purchase flood insurance. However, Texas law does not impose a duty on an insurer to advise an insured on coverage adequacy. See Allied Insurance v. Garcia, 476 S.W.3d 498 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2015, no pet.).

You also stated in your claim that the water came from a burst pipe in the wall. We have photographic evidence and statements from neighbors that the water rose from the ground. Therefore, your inconsistent statement may constitute fraud, and we reserve the right to void the policy if evidence supports that.

You may appeal this denial by submitting a written request to the Texas Department of Insurance within 30 days. Our legal counsel is David H. Patel, Esq., who may be reached at (713) 555-0034 or d.patel@lonestarmutual.com.

Sincerely,

Lone Star Mutual Insurance Company
By: Karen J. Whitaker, Claims Director

cc: David H. Patel, Esq.
    Hon. Judge Samuel T. Garcia (presiding in case cause number 24-001123) – referred to as Judge Garcia.

title: Denial of Life Insurance Claim – Suicide Exclusion
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS
CAUSE NO. PR-24-00088

IN RE: ESTATE OF MARY LOUISE HARRIS (formerly known as Mary Louise Patterson), Deceased.

NOTICE OF DENIAL OF LIFE INSURANCE BENEFITS

TO: Frank David Harris, Personal Representative
2100 Oakwood Street, Dallas, Texas 75201
Phone: (713) 555-7711
Email: fharris@estateattorney.com

Date of Death: February 10, 2024

Dear Mr. Harris:

This letter is to notify you that Sentinel Life Assurance Company denies payment of the death benefit under policy number LA-4589-10, issued to Mary Louise Harris. The policy was applied for on January 15, 2023, and became effective on February 1, 2023. The denial is based on the policy’s suicide exclusion.

The policy provides that if the insured dies by suicide within the first two years from the date of issue, the benefit is limited to a refund of premiums paid. The death certificate, signed by Dr. Ellen S. Park, lists the cause of death as “suicide by firearm.” The date of death, February 10, 2024, is within the two-year contestable period. Therefore, the only amount payable is $2,350, representing the total premiums paid. We have enclosed a check in that amount.

You have contested this decision, citing the case of In re Life Insurance Co. of Texas, 508 S.W.3d 445 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2016, writ denied). However, that case is distinguishable because the insured there had a mental condition that did not meet the legal definition of suicide. Here, the medical examiner’s report and toxicology results unequivocally indicate a self-inflicted injury with intent to die.

Furthermore, your application for benefits states that Mary Louise Harris was in good mental health at the time of application. We have obtained her medical records from Dr. James R. Chen, which show she was being treated for severe depression and had been hospitalized in December 2022. This omission constitutes a material misrepresentation. Under Texas Insurance Code § 705.001, a misrepresentation that materially affects the risk entitles the insurer to void the policy. See also Johnson v. Security Life Ins. Co., 537 S.W.3d 112 (Tex. 2017) (citations omitted).

We also note that the beneficiary designation lists you, Frank Harris, as primary beneficiary. A minor, A.B., is listed as contingent beneficiary. Since the policy is being denied, no benefit is payable to either.

Our legal representative is Thomas J. Miller, Esq., (713) 555-8844, t.miller@sentinelassurance.com. You may seek independent legal advice.

Sincerely,

Sentinel Life Assurance Company
By: Cynthia R. Barnes, Claims Manager

cc: Thomas J. Miller, Esq.
    Judge Rebecca L. Nguyen (presiding probate judge) – referred to as Judge Nguyen.
cited_case_parties: In re Life Insurance Co. of Texas
Johnson v. Security Life Ins. Co.

title: Denial of Health Insurance – Pre-Existing Condition Exclusion
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS
224th JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-CV-01234

MARIA ISABEL SANTOS (maiden name: Maria Isabel Rodriguez), Plaintiff,
vs.
GOLDEN CROSS HEALTHCARE PLAN, INC., Defendant.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

TO: Maria Isabel Santos
8820 Alamo Heights Boulevard, San Antonio, Texas 78209
Phone: (713) 555-9988
Email: misantos@myhealthmail.com

Date of Birth: born on March 14, 1971

Policy ID: GC-77-4521-00

Dear Ms. Santos:

This letter is to notify you that Golden Cross Healthcare Plan, Inc. has denied your claim for coverage of bariatric surgery (gastric bypass) scheduled for April 12, 2024. The denial is based on the policy’s pre-existing condition exclusion.

Your group health plan, issued to your employer, Alamo City Services, became effective on January 1, 2024. The policy contains a 12-month pre-existing condition exclusion for any condition for which medical advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment was recommended or received within the 6-month period ending on the effective date. Your medical records from Dr. Linda G. Foster show that you were diagnosed with morbid obesity (BMI 42) on July 15, 2023, and were referred for bariatric evaluation on August 20, 2023. Both events occurred within the 6-month look-back period. Therefore, the condition is excluded.

You have argued that your condition was not “pre-existing” because you had not yet been formally diagnosed with “obesity-related comorbidities.” However, the policy definition of “pre-existing condition” includes the condition itself. Texas Insurance Code § 1251.002 defines a pre-existing condition as a condition for which medical advice or treatment was recommended or received within the specified period. The Texas Supreme Court, in the case of In re Cigna Healthcare of Texas, 601 S.W.3d 715 (Tex. 2020), upheld a similar exclusion where the diagnosis was made before the policy effective date.

Additionally, you failed to disclose your history of weight-related treatments on your enrollment form. You stated that you had not received any medical advice for weight loss, yet records from your primary care physician show you had been prescribed appetite suppressants in 2023. This is a material misrepresentation, which would also allow us to rescind coverage under Texas Insurance Code § 705.004. See also Peterson v. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, 573 S.W.3d 301 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2018, pet. denied).

We also note that your minor child, A.B., is listed as a dependent on the policy. If you appeal, you may submit evidence that the exclusion does not apply.

Our legal counsel is William J. Hart, Esq., (713) 555-2020, w.hart@goldencross.com. You may also contact the Texas Department of Insurance.

Sincerely,

Golden Cross Healthcare Plan, Inc.
By: Gloria M. Sanchez, Appeals Coordinator

cc: William J. Hart, Esq.
    Judge Michael A. O’Connor (presiding in related matter cause number 24-9876) – referred to as Judge O’Connor.

Enclosures: Claim determination, policy excerpts.

title: Denial of Disability Insurance – Exclusion for Pre-Existing Mental Condition
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TARRANT COUNTY, TEXAS
352nd JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-33321-B

STEVEN MICHAEL COOPER, Plaintiff,
vs.
PRAIRIE VIEW ASSURANCE COMPANY, Defendant.

NOTICE OF DENIAL OF DISABILITY INCOME BENEFITS

TO: Steven Michael Cooper
5601 Lakewood Drive, Fort Worth, Texas 76102
Phone: (713) 555-3344
Email: scooper@worklife.org

Social Security Number (partial): 327-65-XXXX

Date of Birth: born on March 14, 1971

Dear Mr. Cooper:

This letter is to inform you that Prairie View Assurance Company has denied your claim for long-term disability benefits under policy number DI-100-7823, effective July 1, 2022. You stopped working on March 10, 2024, citing severe anxiety and panic attacks. Our denial is based on the policy’s exclusion for disability caused by a pre-existing mental or nervous disorder, and on a material misrepresentation in your application.

Your application stated that you had no history of mental health treatment. However, our review of records from Dr. Rachel S. Kim, a psychiatrist, revealed that you were treated for generalized anxiety disorder from February 2021 through May 2022, ending just before the policy effective date. This condition is a “pre-existing condition” under the policy, as you received treatment within the 24-month look-back period. The policy defines a pre-existing condition as any condition for which medical treatment was received within 24 months before the policy date. Therefore, the disability is excluded.

Furthermore, you certified on the application that you had never been diagnosed with a mental disorder. This is a material misrepresentation. Under Texas Insurance Code § 705.002, the insurer may void the policy if the misrepresentation would have caused the insurer to deny coverage or charge a higher premium. The Texas Court of Appeals, in the case of In re Guardian Life Insurance Co., 462 S.W.3d 543 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 2015, no pet.), held that a false statement regarding prior mental health treatment voids coverage. See also Barnes v. Metropolitan Life Ins. Co., 548 S.W.3d 681 (Tex. 2018).

You have also listed a minor dependent, A.B., on your policy as a beneficiary for a small accidental death rider, but that does not affect this denial.

Our legal representative is Jonathan P. Wells, Esq., (713) 555-6677, j.wells@prairieviewassurance.com. You may appeal this decision within 180 days by submitting additional medical evidence.

Sincerely,

Prairie View Assurance Company
By: Laura B. Daniels, Senior Claims Analyst

cc: Jonathan P. Wells, Esq.
    Judge Karen L. Stephens (presiding in related appeal cause number 24-5555) – referred to as Judge Stephens.

Barnes v. Metropolitan Life Ins. Co.
